analysis.title: The 720: Daikin upgrade, US Semis, Nvidia, China Tax, Basic Materials, Furukawa Electric, Wuxi AppTec, JX Advanced Metals, ANZ Telcos
key_insights: Daikin upgraded to Buy from Neutral, 12m TP raised to ¥30,000 from ¥26,000. FY3/27 and FY3/29 operating profit estimates raised to ¥470 bn and ¥550 bn. Drivers are front-loaded demand and price increases in Japan, cooling demand and inventory restocking in Europe, and mix and inverter growth in the Americas.
GS expects the post-rush volume decline in Japan in FY3/28 to be offset by Daikin's European and Americas tailwinds.

Kurita Water downgraded to Neutral from Buy, 12m TP cut to ¥6,000 from ¥8,600. A higher share of lower-margin facilities business and rising materials and labor costs reduce visibility on electronics profitability. GS forecasts FY3/27-FY3/29 business profits of ¥40 bn, ¥71 bn and ¥74 bn.
US semiconductors fell 13% in the recent sector selloff on post-election uncertainty about the pace of datacenter builds. GS calls the group oversold with compelling risk/reward.
GS's power-based analysis projects global AI infrastructure capex of about $1.3 trillion in 2027, with a baseline of 35 GW of datacenter deployments largely already in progress.

GS prefers Nvidia and Broadcom for AI compute and Applied Materials and Lam Research for semiconductor capital equipment. It sees attractive entry points in Samsung and SK Hynix as they approach tangible book value.
Nvidia 3Q preview (Buy, 12m TP $300 maintained): GS expects solid 3Q results and 4Q guidance above Street, driven by better margins. Its 3Q and 4Q EPS estimates are both 6% above consensus.
Expected focus on Nvidia's call: visibility into datacenter power and shell capacity through 2028, the sustainability of external funding for AI infrastructure, and agentic-driven CPU demand.

China tax enforcement is seen as a structural trend and a major drag on growth this year. Stricter collection explains about Rmb300bn of unexplained tax revenue growth, and with social security collections the boost is Rmb500bn versus 2021.

The Rmb500bn gain does not cover a Rmb2.8tn structural shortfall from falling land sales, debt servicing and pension subsidies, leaving an estimated Rmb2.3tn funding gap. GS expects enforcement to persist, which could end the decade of Augmented Fiscal Deficits above 10% of GDP.

China basic materials estimates refreshed. 2026 steelmaker earnings cut by 10-80% and cement net profit by 7-18%. LME copper forecasts for 2026-2027 raised by 2-12% on tighter ex-US deficits. Buy ratings reiterated on Zijin (on CL) and CMOC.

NYPCB (Buy, TP NT$2,700): management guides 4Q26 revenue up about 20% QoQ with ABF substrate gross margin above 40%, faster than GS expected. ABF ASPs are expected to rise 10-15% QoQ in 4Q26 and keep rising through 2027. GS sees ABF gross margins reaching 55-60% in 2H27.

Furukawa Electric (Buy) posted a 2Q beat and raised FY3/27 sales and operating profit guidance to ¥1.57 tn and ¥136 bn. GS raised FY3/27-FY3/29 operating profit estimates by 11%/5%/1% and cut the 12m TP to ¥4,100 on a margin-based valuation framework and lower market multiples.

Furukawa's visibility is improving through long-term agreements with double-digit price revisions and volume shortfall compensation, plus ramps in water cooling modules and high-performance copper foil.

Ajinomoto (Buy, TP ¥6,700) 2Q business profit of ¥48.5 bn (+23% yoy) missed consensus. Full-year profit guidance was raised to ¥210 bn from ¥202 bn and the DPS to ¥52. Functional materials profit rose 86% yoy, while frozen foods and bio-pharma services posted unexpected losses and there was no buyback.

Softbank Corp (Buy) reported in-line 2Q operating profit of ¥339.8 bn and raised full-year operating profit guidance to ¥1,160 bn from ¥1,100 bn, mainly on the financial segment. GS expects profit growth to accelerate in 2H on mobile price hikes, corporate AI solutions, commerce and PayPay.

JX Advanced Metals (Buy, TP ¥5,160 maintained): 2Q operating profit rose 71% YoY to ¥69.3bn, beating expectations. FY3/27 operating profit guidance was raised 10% to ¥255.0bn, with Semiconductor Materials guidance up 20% to ¥73.0bn. Target operations run near 90% utilization and the company is expanding capacity.
Jiangsu King's Luck Brewery (Buy) 12m TP raised to Rmb37.6 from Rmb33. 2026-2028 sales estimates rose 6-7% and earnings estimates 5-8% on Danya demand and share gains in Jiangsu.

Namura Shipbuilding (Buy, TP ¥6,000) 2Q operating profit of ¥6.2 bn missed GS's ¥8.8 bn estimate. Full-year operating profit guidance was raised to ¥32.0 bn from ¥29.0 bn and the dividend plan to ¥70/share. Backlog covers three and a half years.

Life360 (Buy, TP A$30.95) 3Q26 revenue of $174m and Adjusted EBITDA of $34.6m beat GS expectations on record Paying Circles growth of 189k. MAUs rose 5.3m sequentially to 18% yoy growth, but the skew toward international users was slightly disappointing. FY26 revenue guidance midpoint was raised slightly to $673m and Adjusted EBITDA held at $135m.
WuXi AppTec (Buy, TPs HK$251/Rmb213) Investor Day: AI-driven drug discovery is seen as an emerging growth driver for early-stage CRO demand, and commercial GLP-1 projects rose from two to three.

GS initiated on ANZ telcos. It sees low-earth-orbit satellite as a long-term terminal risk, not a near-term earnings threat, and estimates A$900mn in gross annual AI cost savings for incumbents. Initiations: Superloop Buy, Telstra Neutral, TPG Telecom Sell, Aussie Broadband Sell, Spark New Zealand Neutral.

China spirits: leading brands are embracing Double 11 online and livestream sales with discounts. High-end wholesale prices stay soft, with Feitian Moutai original case at Rmb1,705 per bottle. Distillers prioritize destocking and price preservation over volume, and GS expects pressure into 2027.

EU multi-industry: US midterm results add timing risk to datacenter pipelines through possible moratoria in Democratic-won states. GS expects a longer capex cycle rather than a smaller market. Prysmian and Wartsila could benefit from transmission and behind-the-meter generation spending, and derated Legrand is highlighted.

Global strategy: AI infrastructure is 15% of the STOXX 600 versus 40% of the S&P 500 and drives 2pp of expected 9% earnings growth in 2027. GS favors companies with durable moats as Phase 2 infrastructure capex growth peaks and sees a contrarian opportunity in de-rated Phase 3 software and IT services.

Estee Lauder (Buy on CL, TP $129 reiterated): after its China Capital Markets Event, GS is incrementally positive. FY30 targets are mid-single-digit organic sales growth and double-digit adjusted EPS growth, and management expects 30% of global launches to come from the China Innovation Center.
Graphic: based only on capacity under construction, US data center capacity rises from 65GW-gross in 2026 to 143GW-gross by 2030, with net additions of 33/37/8/0GW-gross in 2027/28/29/30.
